reference_memory.normal_pattern: The normal pattern is a piecewise-constant staircase with a consistent upward trend, composed of flat plateaus separated by sharp, near-vertical step increases. Each plateau lasts approximately 19 points (1 cycle), matching the estimated period of 19; longer windows (3P, 5P) contain 3 or 5 such cycles respectively. The steps occur roughly every 19 points, with minor jitter in exact step timing (±1–2 points) across candidates. Plateau levels increase monotonically across the series, reflecting the underlying linear+quadratic trend in the full time series. Amplitude within each plateau is extremely low: MAD ≤0.0185, 90% amplitude ≤0.08, and roughness/curvature are zero—indicating no oscillatory or noisy dynamics, only quantized-level stability. Peaks are the top edges of steps (flat tops), troughs are the bottom edges (flat bottoms); both are horizontal segments, not rounded extrema. Noise is negligible—values are nearly constant within plateaus, with only tiny quantization-like fluctuations (<0.001). The pattern is highly stable across candidates despite differing absolute levels (medians range from −1.34 to +1.27), confirming that level shifts are part of the expected trend, not anomalies. Acceptable variation includes: (1) ±1–2 point shift in step timing, (2) slight differences in step height (0.01–0.02 per step), (3) minor plateau length variation (18–20 points), and (4) consistent monotonic progression without reversals or overshoots.

reference_profiles.description: A single-cycle (1P) segment showing two flat plateaus connected by one sharp step at index ~3–4, then another step at ~15–16. Very low amplitude (MAD=0.00025), near-perfect flatness, minimal noise. Represents the finest-grained morphology of the staircase.

Three-cycle (3P) segment with three plateaus and two intermediate steps, plus a final step near the end. Plateaus are slightly noisier (MAD=0.011) but still flat; step heights ~0.01–0.02. Matches the 19-point cadence well; step positions align with multiples of ~19 (e.g., ~58, ~116 global offset).

Another 3P segment, similar to ref 1 but with higher baseline (median=0.476) and slightly smaller step heights. Plateaus equally flat; step timing again aligns with ~19-point intervals. Minor deviation: one plateau appears 20 points long vs. 19, but within acceptable variation.

Five-cycle (5P) segment showing five plateaus and four steps, confirming the repeating motif over longer horizon. Step heights vary slightly (0.01–0.02), plateau lengths mostly 19 points, with one possibly 20-point plateau. Highest MAD (0.0185) and amplitude (0.08) due to cumulative trend, but morphology remains identical: flat plateaus, sharp steps, no curvature.
distinctive_features: largest absolute values but same shape

reference_memory.selection_guidance: Prefer reference 0 for queries with ≤20 points or when high-resolution step detection is needed (e.g., identifying early-step anomalies). Use references 1 or 2 for queries of ~50–60 points to match 3-cycle morphology and moderate noise tolerance. Use reference 3 for queries >80 points or when assessing long-horizon consistency; its 5-cycle structure helps detect missing/extra steps. All references agree on step cadence (~19), so mismatched step timing (e.g., steps at 10, 30, 50) should trigger anomaly suspicion regardless of chosen reference.
uncertainties: Exact step height distribution (whether deterministic or stochastic) cannot be confirmed from 4 samples
Whether plateau length strictly equals period (19) or allows ±1 variation in all contexts
Potential for very rare flat segments without steps (i.e., single-cycle anomalies) is unobserved and thus undefined
